messages.text: Verstappen wins wild Las Vegas GP as Ferraris collide again

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen produced a remarkable drive to win a wild Las Vegas Grand Prix that saw him withstand extreme pressure from George Russell and Kimi Antonelli before a late Mercedes collapse.
metadata.content: Las Vegas GP: Max Verstappen wins wild race as Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collide again | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Las Vegas GP: Max Verstappen wins wild race as Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collide again Max Verstappen wins wild Las Vegas Grand Prix; Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri claim double podium for McLaren after late Mercedes collapse saw George Russell and Kimi Antonelli drop back; Charles Leclerc penalised for causing collision with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton Sunday 22 November 2026 05:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Max Verstappen produced a remarkable drive to win a wild Las Vegas Grand Prix that saw him withstand extreme pressure from George Russell and Kimi Antonelli before a late Mercedes collapse. Pole-sitter Verstappen retained the lead at the start but the enormous power of a slipstream on the long straights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit made it impossible for the Dutchman to pull clear, and resulted in 34 changes of the lead and well over 300 total overtakes in the 50-lap race. First Russell, and then later newly crowned world champion Antonelli were each able to pass Verstappen on multiple occasions but the Red Bull driver calmly retook the lead within a few corners every time, expertly managing the deployment of his power. messages.text: 'Completely unacceptable! - Vasseur slams Leclerc for Hamilton collision

metadata.summary: Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur blamed Charles Leclerc for a "completely unacceptable" collision with team-mate Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur blames Charles Leclerc for 'unacceptable' collision with Lewis Hamilton in Las Vegas GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur blames Charles Leclerc for 'unacceptable' collision with Lewis Hamilton in Las Vegas GP The Ferrari team-mates clashed on track once again, just weeks after their costly collision in Mexico City derailed the team’s race; Charles Leclerc punished by stewards and blamed by team boss Frederic Vasseur after spinning Lewis Hamilton in battle over sixth place Sunday 22 November 2026 08:01, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton spins after contact with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, which led to a 10-second penalty for the latter at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur blamed Charles Leclerc for a "completely unacceptable" collision with team-mate Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Ferrari drivers made contact when battling over sixth place with 12 laps remaining in a breathless, frenzied race in which the team were attempting to recover from a poor qualifying when both drivers were knocked out in Q2. Hamilton was spun around in the Turn Seven-collision, dropping to 10th in the order. Leclerc was found to be at fault by race stewards, who imposed a 10-second penalty on him. Iraola has been in charge at Anfield for less than six months after replacing Arne Slot in June following Liverpool's dismal Premier League title defence last season under the Dutchman. The then champions could only manage an underwhelming fifth-place finish, 24 points worse off than when winning the league in 2024-25, with Slot paying with his job as a result.
